### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The AI generation service (`backend/src/app/modules/ai_model/ai_model.service.ts`) calls Gemini directly through `raceGenerationWithTimeout` with no concurrency cap. Each call can run up to 60 seconds. A burst of requests handled by one server instance therefore starts an unbounded number of concurrent 60-second Gemini calls, which is a cost / quota exhaustion vector against the Gemini API.

The repo already contains a concurrency queue for exactly this purpose, `backend/src/services/storyRequestQueue.ts` (caps concurrent AI calls to `AI_CONCURRENCY`, default 3), added in #1055 / PR #1056. However, it is never imported or used anywhere, so it is currently dead code and provides no protection.

The per-IP rate limiter (5 free generations per day, MongoDB-backed) already exists and bounds how often any single IP can call the endpoints, but it does not cap how many generations run concurrently inside one instance.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open `backend/src/app/modules/ai_model/ai_model.service.ts`. Every generation goes through `raceGenerationWithTimeout(...)` with no concurrency control.
2. Search the codebase for `storyQueue` or `storyRequestQueue`. It is defined in `backend/src/services/storyRequestQueue.ts` but has no importers, so the queue is never used.

### Expected behavior

Gemini generation calls should pass through the existing `storyRequestQueue`, so concurrent external AI calls per instance are capped at `AI_CONCURRENCY` (default 3) regardless of incoming traffic.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `backend/src/app/modules/ai_model/ai_model.service.ts`
- Queue: `backend/src/services/storyRequestQueue.ts`

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. Backend concurrency control.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

Three of the five free (guest) AI endpoints in `backend/src/app/modules/ai_model/ai_model.controller.ts` set the `userId` guest-tracking cookie with no security flags:

- `aiFreeModelRemix`
- `aiFreeModelTranslate`
- `aiFreeModelChat`

Each does `res.cookie("userId", userId, { maxAge: 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 })` with no `httpOnly`, `secure`, or `sameSite`. The other two endpoints (`aiFreeModelGenerate`, `aiFreeModelAlternateEndings`) already use the shared `setGuestUserIdCookie` helper from `utils/cookie.util.ts`, which applies `httpOnly`, `secure` (in production), and `sameSite`. So the cookie handling is inconsistent, and on three endpoints the guest cookie is readable by client-side JavaScript and is not protected against cross-site sending.

This is the cookie-flags part. The separate concern that the guest id itself is generated with `Math.random()` is already tracked in #1275, so this issue does not cover that.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call one of `POST /ai-model/free/remix`, `/free/translate`, or `/free/chat` as a guest (no auth) with no existing `userId` cookie.
2. Inspect the `Set-Cookie` response header. The `userId` cookie is set without `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, or `SameSite`.
3. Compare with the free generate/alternate-endings endpoints, where the same cookie is set with those flags.

### Expected behavior

All five free endpoints should set the guest `userId` cookie through the shared `setGuestUserIdCookie` helper so the cookie consistently carries `httpOnly`, `secure` (in production), and `sameSite`.

payload.author: Anexus5919
payload.body:
### Current Situation

The Express app (`backend/src/app.ts`) already applies `helmet()`, `trust proxy`, and a global rate limiter (the security-headers/rate-limit part is tracked separately in #1269). However, three standard production middlewares are still missing:

- No response compression, so JSON and text responses are sent uncompressed.
- No request id, so a single request cannot be correlated across log lines, and a client cannot reference a specific failing request.
- No HTTP request access logging (method, path, status, latency).

### Proposed Improvement

- Add a request-id middleware that assigns every request a stable id. It honors an upstream `X-Request-Id` header when present (useful behind a proxy or Vercel) and otherwise generates a uuid, then echoes it back in the `X-Request-Id` response header. `uuid` is already a dependency, so this needs no new package.
- Add `compression()` so responses are gzip/deflate compressed.
- Add HTTP request logging (`morgan`) that includes the request id and is routed through the existing `logger.util`, so it honors `disable_logs` on serverless (Vercel) and stays consistent with the rest of the app's logging.

This intentionally does not re-add `helmet`, since `helmet()` is already present (see #1269).

### Benefits

- Smaller payloads and faster responses for clients (compression).
- End-to-end traceability of each request via `X-Request-Id`, which also lets clients report the exact request that failed.
- Visibility into method, path, status, and latency for every request during development.

### Area of Improvement

Performance and Developer Experience.

### Additional context

A PR is ready for this.

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

payload.author: Anexus5919
payload.body:
**Describe the bug**

`backend/src/server.ts` calls `dns.setServers(["1.1.1.1", "8.8.8.8"])` unconditionally at module import time. This is a process-wide global side effect that overrides the platform DNS resolver for every lookup the backend makes.

On Vercel and most hosts the platform resolver works fine, and forcing public resolvers can break resolution of private or internal hostnames if internal services are added later. The call was introduced in a general refactor commit, not as a deliberate DNS fix, and the `dns` import is used only for this one line. This is a configuration anti-pattern (unconditional global side effect at import), not a security hole.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open `backend/src/server.ts`.
2. The first executable statement after the imports is `dns.setServers(["1.1.1.1", "8.8.8.8"])`.
3. It runs on every boot regardless of environment, replacing the host resolver globally.

**Expected behavior**

The backend should use the platform DNS resolver by default. A custom resolver override should be opt-in (configurable), not forced on every deployment.

**Screenshots**

N/A.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
  - OS: N/A (server-side configuration)
  - Browser: N/A
  - Version: N/A

**Additional context**

Suggested fix: make the override opt-in via a new optional `DNS_SERVERS` env var (comma-separated). Only call `dns.setServers` when it is set; otherwise use the platform resolver. This removes the unconditional global side effect while keeping an escape hatch for environments that genuinely need custom DNS (for example certain MongoDB Atlas SRV setups). Document `DNS_SERVERS` as optional in `.env.example`. I have a PR ready for this.
payload.title: [BUG]: server.ts overrides global DNS resolvers unconditionally at import time

payload.author: Anexus5919
payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

In `backend/src/server.ts`, when `DISABLE_LOGS=true` or running on Vercel (`VERCEL=1`), the startup code replaces every console method with a no-op, including `console.warn` and `console.error`:

```ts
if (config.disable_logs) {
  const noop = () => undefined;
  console.log = noop;
  console.info = noop;
  console.debug = noop;
  console.warn = noop;
  console.error = noop;
}
```

Because `config.disable_logs` is true on Vercel by default, this silences the error channel in production. Many fire-and-forget paths report failures via `console.error`, for example `GamificationService.updateDailyStreak(...).catch(console.error)` and similar handlers in `auth.service.ts`, `post.service.ts`, and `ai_model.controller.ts` (about a dozen `catch(console.error)` call sites). With `console.error` stubbed out, those failures vanish with no trace in the Vercel function logs, making production issues effectively undebuggable.

This maps to CWE-778 (Insufficient Logging).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy on Vercel (or set `DISABLE_LOGS=true`).
2. Trigger any fire-and-forget failure (for example a gamification update that rejects).
3. Observe that nothing is logged, because `console.error` is a no-op.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `backend/src/server.ts`

### Suggested fix

Silence only the verbose channels (`console.log`, `console.info`, `console.debug`) and keep `console.warn` and `console.error` working, so warnings and errors still appear in the platform logs.

A PR is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

Lower the name minimum to 2 consistently across the Mongoose schema, the register Zod validator, and the signup form, so two-character names are accepted and the three layers stay aligned (avoiding a repeat of the #1456 mismatch).

payload.author: Anexus5919
payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

Access tokens are issued with a very long default lifetime. `JWT_EXPIRES_IN` defaults to `60d` in `backend/.env.example` and the README, and `issueAccessToken` in `auth.service.ts` uses `config.jwt.expires_in` directly. Although `/login` was recently changed to use `15m` (or `30d` with `rememberMe`), the other token-issuing paths still use the long default:

- `register`
- `googleLogin`
- `resetPassword`
- `refreshToken`

The `refreshToken` case is the most significant: every refresh re-issues a 60-day access token, which defeats the purpose of the short-lived-access-token plus refresh-rotation design that was just added. Combined with the access token being stored in `localStorage` (see the open #1075 about XSS token theft) and no per-token revocation, a single stolen access token is usable for up to 60 days.

Industry practice is a short access-token lifetime (minutes to about an hour) with longer sessions provided by refresh-token rotation, which this codebase now supports.

This maps to CWE-613 (Insufficient Session Expiration).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register, log in with Google, reset a password, or call `/auth/refresh-token`.
2. Decode the returned access token and observe the `exp` claim is about 60 days out (per the `JWT_EXPIRES_IN=60d` default).

### Environment (if relevant)

- Files: `backend/src/app/modules/auth/auth.service.ts`, `backend/.env.example`, `README.md`

### Suggested fix

Default the access token to a short lifetime everywhere: change `JWT_EXPIRES_IN` to `15m` in `.env.example` and the README, and make `issueAccessToken` fall back to `15m` when the env value is unset, so register / googleLogin / resetPassword / refreshToken all issue short tokens. The longer `rememberMe` session on login and the long refresh-token lifetime are unaffected.

A PR is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

Several pages in the application perform asynchronous API requests to load user data, analytics, community content, and other dynamic resources. However, these requests are not consistently cancelled when a user navigates away from the page before the request completes.

As a result, API calls may continue running in the background even after the associated component has unmounted. This can lead to stale responses being processed, unnecessary network usage, increased backend load, and potential race conditions where outdated data overwrites newer state.

This behavior becomes more noticeable when users rapidly switch between pages, repeatedly trigger data-fetching actions, or use slower network connections.


### Steps to reproduce

- Cancel in-flight API requests when a component unmounts.
- Abort stale requests during route transitions.
- Prevent outdated responses from updating application state.
- Standardize request cleanup patterns across the codebase.
- Improve performance and reduce unnecessary backend traffic.

### Environment (if relevant)

- Use AbortController for fetch-based requests.
- Add cleanup functions inside useEffect hooks.
- Ensure pending requests are aborted during route changes.
- Create reusable utilities/hooks for request cancellation where appropriate.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

In `frontend/src/App.tsx`, the dashboard child routes have inconsistent role guards.

- `/dashboard/users` and `/dashboard/writers` sit directly under the outer `ProtectedRoute allowedRoles={ALL_ROLES}` guard, so any logged-in user (including a plain `user`) can navigate to them. The backend correctly restricts the underlying endpoints to `ADMIN` / `SUPER_ADMIN` (`/user/lists`, `/user/writer-application-list`, `/user/approve-writer-application`), so a non-admin sees an empty or failing admin page, but the admin-only UI should not render at all.
- Conversely, `/dashboard/settings` is wrapped in `ProtectedRoute allowedRoles={[USER, WRITER]}`, which excludes `ADMIN` and `SUPER_ADMIN`. Admins cannot reach their own settings page.

This maps to CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization) on the client side. It is defense in depth, since the backend already enforces the real authorization, but the route guards should match.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Log in as a plain `user`. Navigate to `/dashboard/users` or `/dashboard/writers`. The admin page renders (then fails to load data) instead of redirecting.
2. Log in as an `admin`. Navigate to `/dashboard/settings`. You are redirected away from your own settings page.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `frontend/src/App.tsx`

### Suggested fix

- Wrap `users` and `writers` in a `ProtectedRoute allowedRoles={ELEVATED_ADMIN_ROLES}` (the existing `[ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN]` constant), matching the backend.
- Widen `settings` to `allowedRoles={ALL_ROLES}` so every authenticated role can reach their settings.

A PR is attached.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

`frontend/src/services/auth.service.ts` contains unresolved merge duplicates that make it fail to parse. A merge commit (`c76f811`, "resolve merge conflicts with upstream") kept both sides of several conflicts interleaved instead of choosing one:

- `export type AuthUserInfo = {` on line 10 has no body and is immediately followed by unrelated code, and a second complete `type AuthUserInfo` is declared later.
- `buildUserInfo` is declared twice; the first copy is left unterminated.
- The expiry check inside `getValidDecodedToken` is duplicated.
- `getToken` is exported twice.

Because of the dangling `= {` and duplicate declarations, TypeScript cannot parse the file, which contributes to the failing frontend Type Check and build. Locally this file alone produces about 20 cascading parse errors.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the frontend type check: `npm exec -w story-spark-ai-frontend -- tsc -b --noEmit`.
2. Observe a cluster of `TS1005` / `TS1131` parse errors originating in `frontend/src/services/auth.service.ts` (lines 10, 40, etc.).

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

`frontend/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` writes the full current URL, including the query string, into a `localStorage` diagnostics log (`app_error_log`) when a render error is caught:

```ts
url: typeof window !== "undefined" ? window.location.href : "",
```

`window.location.href` includes the query string, so if a URL ever carries sensitive values in its params (a preview or reset token, `?ref=`, `?email=`, etc.), those are persisted to `localStorage` and remain there across logout, readable by anyone with access to the browser profile. The log is also never cleared on logout.

This maps to CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Visit a route with a query string while logged in, for example `/something?token=abc`.
2. Trigger a render error so the ErrorBoundary catches it.
3. Inspect `localStorage["app_error_log"]`; the stored entry's `url` contains the full query string and persists after logout.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `frontend/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx`

### Suggested fix

Log only the origin and pathname (drop the query string), and clear `app_error_log` on logout. The attached PR does the first part (`window.location.origin + window.location.pathname`). The logout cleanup is deferred until a separate corruption in `auth.service.ts` (where `removeUserInfo` lives) is repaired; that file does not currently parse and is filed separately.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

**`getLatestPosts` and `getFeaturedPosts` have duplicate `.limit()` calls where the second overrides the first, causing incorrect result counts.**

In `backend/src/app/modules/post/post.service.ts`:

**`getLatestPosts` (lines 216-226):**
```typescript
const res = await Post.find({ isDeleted: { $ne: true } })
  .sort({ createdAt: -1 })
  .limit(3)                       // ← intended: return 3 latest posts
  .populate("author", "name email createdAt")
  .limit(50)                      // ← OVERRIDES the previous limit(3)!
  .populate("author", "name createdAt profile.bio")
  ...
```

**`getFeaturedPosts` (lines 238-251):**
```typescript
const res = await Post.find({
  isFeaturedPost: true,
  isDeleted: { $ne: true },
})
  .sort({ createdAt: -1, updatedBy: -1 })
  .limit(3)                       // ← intended: return 3 featured posts
  .populate("author", "name email createdAt")
  .limit(10)                      // ← OVERRIDES the previous limit(3)!
  .populate("author", "name createdAt profile.bio")
  ...
```

In Mongoose, when `.limit()` is called multiple times in a query chain, **only the last `.limit()` value takes effect**. The earlier `.limit(3)` is completely ignored.

This means:
- `GET /api/v1/post/latest-posts` returns **up to 50 posts** instead of the intended 3
- `GET /api/v1/post/featured-posts` returns **up to 10 posts** instead of the intended 3

These methods also populate `author` twice with different field selections, where only the last `.populate("author", ...)` is applied.

### Expected Behavior

- `getLatestPosts` should return exactly 3 most recent posts
- `getFeaturedPosts` should return exactly 3 featured posts

### Actual Behavior

- `getLatestPosts` returns up to 50 posts (the second `.limit(50)` overrides `.limit(3)`)
- `getFeaturedPosts` returns up to 10 posts (the second `.limit(10)` overrides `.limit(3)`)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create more than 3 published posts in the database
2. Call `GET /api/v1/post/latest-posts`
3. Observe that more than 3 posts are returned (up to 50)
4. Mark more than 3 posts as featured
5. Call `GET /api/v1/post/featured-posts`
6. Observe that more than 3 posts are returned (up to 10)

### Suggested Fix

Remove the duplicate `.limit()` and `.populate("author")` calls:

```typescript
// getLatestPosts
const res = await Post.find({ isDeleted: { $ne: true } })
  .sort({ createdAt: -1 })
  .limit(3)
  .populate("author", "name createdAt profile.bio")
  .populate({
    path: "reactions",
    populate: { path: "userId", select: "_id" },
  })
  .populate("bookmarks", "_id");

// getFeaturedPosts
const res = await Post.find({
  isFeaturedPost: true,
  isDeleted: { $ne: true },
})
  .sort({ createdAt: -1, updatedBy: -1 })
  .limit(3)
  .populate("author", "name createdAt profile.bio")
  .populate({
    path: "reactions",
    populate: { path: "userId", select: "_id" },
  })
  .populate("bookmarks", "_id");
```

### Impact

- The "Latest Stories" section on the homepage may show too many posts (up to 50 instead of 3)
- The "Featured Stories" section shows up to 10 instead of the intended 3
- Unnecessary database load from returning more documents than needed
- Extra data transferred over the wire for each request
- These are likely hotspots — called on every homepage load

### Environment

- **File**: `backend/src/app/modules/post/post.service.ts` (lines 216-226, 238-251)
- **Branch**: `main`
- **Framework**: Mongoose / Express.js

### Record

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct
- [x] I want to work on this issue

Hey @ronisarkarexe! I'm a GSSoC'26 contributor. Found this bug where duplicate `.limit()` calls make the latest/featured posts endpoints return wrong counts. Would love to clean it up! 🚀
payload.title: BUG: Duplicate .limit() calls in getLatestPosts and getFeaturedPosts — second limit overrides the first, returning wrong post counts

### What happened?

**The `getCommentsByPostId` function has an empty body — it always throws a ReferenceError.**

In `backend/src/app/modules/comment/comment.service.ts:45-47`:

```typescript
const getCommentsByPostId = async (postId: string) => {
main
};
```

The function body contains only the string literal `main` (a leftover placeholder from development/a merge artifact). Since `main` is not a defined variable in scope, calling this function will throw a `ReferenceError: main is not defined`.

This means **every request to `GET /api/v1/comment/get-comments/:postId` returns a 500 Internal Server Error**. The entire comment listing feature is broken — no post on the platform can display its comments.

### Expected Behavior

`GET /api/v1/comment/get-comments/:postId` should return all comments for the given post, populated with author information and sorted by creation date.

### Actual Behavior

The endpoint crashes with an unhandled `ReferenceError: main is not defined`, returning a 500 error to the client.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the backend server
2. Create a post and add a comment to it
3. Send a request to `GET /api/v1/comment/get-comments/:postId`

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:5000/api/v1/comment/get-comments/somePostId
# Returns: 500 Internal Server Error
# Expected: Array of comments for the post
```

### Suggested Fix

Replace the placeholder with the actual implementation:

```typescript
const getCommentsByPostId = async (postId: string) => {
  const comments = await Comment.find({ postId: new Types.ObjectId(postId) })
    .populate("userId", "name email profile.avatarUrl")
    .sort({ createdAt: -1 });
  return comments;
};
```

This requires importing `Comment` and `Types` at the top of the file if not already present.

### Impact

- **CRITICAL**: The comment listing feature is completely non-functional
- Any post detail page that tries to load comments will show an error state
- Users cannot read any comments on any story
- The comment system is reduced to write-only (comments can be created but never read back)

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

**Any authenticated user can mark any post as "featured"** — the `PATCH /api/v1/post/featured/:postId` endpoint uses `auth()` with **no role restrictions**, and the service layer performs **no ownership or authorization check**.

In `backend/src/app/modules/post/post.router.ts:37-41`:

```typescript
router.patch(
  "/featured/:postId",
  auth(),                          // ⚠️ No role argument — any authenticated user passes
  PostController.doFeaturedPosts
);
```

The `auth()` middleware (line 42 of `auth.middleware.ts`) only checks role restrictions when roles are provided:
```typescript
if (requiredRole.length && !requiredRole.includes(verifiedUser.role)) {
  throw new ApiError(httpStatus.FORBIDDEN, "Forbidden");
}
```

With `auth()`, `requiredRole` is empty (`[]`), so the role check is **skipped entirely**.

Then in the service layer (`post.service.ts:261-275`), `doFeaturedPosts` only takes a `postId` — it never checks if the caller is the post author or an admin:

```typescript
const doFeaturedPosts = async (postId: string) => {
  const res = await Post.findOneAndUpdate(
    { _id: postId, isDeleted: { $ne: true } },
    { isFeaturedPost: true },
    { new: true }
  );
  return res;
};
```

**A regular user with the `USER` role can feature any post on the platform**, including posts they don't own. This is a privilege escalation / authorization bypass.

### Expected Behavior

Only users with `ADMIN` or `SUPER_ADMIN` roles should be able to mark posts as featured. The endpoint should either:
- Restrict to `ADMIN` / `SUPER_ADMIN` roles, OR
- Check that the authenticated user owns the post (writer features their own) OR is an admin

### Actual Behavior

Any authenticated user (including newly registered `USER` role accounts) can set `isFeaturedPost: true` on any post.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register a new account (gets `USER` role)
2. Obtain an auth token
3. Find any post's ID on the platform
4. Send `PATCH /api/v1/post/featured/:postId` with the token
5. Observe the post is marked as featured — even though the user is not an admin
6. Check `GET /api/v1/post/featured-posts` — the post now appears there

### Suggested Fix

Add role restriction to the route in `post.router.ts:37-41`:

```typescript
router.patch(
  "/featured/:postId",
  auth(ENUM_USER_ROLE.ADMIN, ENUM_USER_ROLE.SUPER_ADMIN),
  PostController.doFeaturedPosts
);
```

### Impact

- Unauthorized users can manipulate the "Featured Posts" section displayed on the homepage
- The credibility of featured content is undermined
- An attacker could promote low-quality or inappropriate content to the featured section
- This is a direct authorization bypass (OWASP A01: Broken Access Control)

### Environment

- **File**: `backend/src/app/modules/post/post.router.ts` (lines 37-41)
- **File**: `backend/src/app/modules/post/post.service.ts` (lines 261-275)
- **Branch**: `main`
- **Framework**: Express.js

- [x] I want to work on this issue

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

**`GET /api/v1/post/tag/:tag` is unreachable** — the route is shadowed by `GET /api/v1/post/:id` which is registered first.

In `backend/src/app/modules/post/post.router.ts`, the routes are defined in this order:

```
router.get("/:id", ...)           // Line 43 — matches ANY single path segment
router.get("/tag/:tag", ...)     // Line 48 — NEVER reached
```

Express routes are matched **in registration order**. When a client sends `GET /api/v1/post/tag/fantasy`, Express matches it against `/:id` first (treating `"tag"` as the `:id` parameter), and `PostController.getSinglePost` is invoked with `req.params.id = "tag"` instead of `PostController.getPostsByTag` with `req.params.tag = "fantasy"`. The `getPostsByTag` controller and service code is effectively **dead code** — it can never be reached through a real HTTP request.

Additionally, because `getSinglePost` performs a `findOne({ _id: "tag" })` lookup, it returns a 404 or a wrong document, giving the user a broken experience when they try to filter stories by genre.

### Expected Behavior

`GET /api/v1/post/tag/fantasy` should return all posts tagged with "fantasy". Specific routes (`/tag/:tag`, `/latest-posts`, `/featured-posts`) should be registered **before** the generic `/:id` wildcard route.

### Actual Behavior

`GET /api/v1/post/tag/fantasy` is intercepted by `GET /api/v1/post/:id`, which tries to find a post with `_id = "tag"` and either returns a 404 or an unrelated document.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the backend server
2. Send a request to `GET /api/v1/post/tag/fantasy`
3. Observe that `getSinglePost` is invoked instead of `getPostsByTag`
4. The response is a 404 (no post with `_id = "tag"`) instead of posts filtered by tag

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:5000/api/v1/post/tag/fantasy | jq .
# Returns: { "success": false, "message": "Post not found" }
# Expected: Posts filtered by tag "fantasy"
```

### Root Cause

The generic wildcard route `/:id` is placed at line 43, before the more specific `/tag/:tag` route at line 48. In Express, route specificity is determined by **registration order**, not by route pattern specificity. All static/specific routes must be registered before the wildcard.

### Suggested Fix

Move all specific named routes (`/latest-posts`, `/featured-posts`, `/tag/:tag`) **above** the generic `/:id` wildcard route in `post.router.ts`. The new ordering should be:

```
GET  /latest-posts       → PostController.getLatestPosts
GET  /featured-posts     → PostController.getFeaturedPosts
GET  /tag/:tag           → PostController.getPostsByTag
GET  /:id                → PostController.getSinglePost       (wildcard last)
PATCH /:id               → PostController.updatePost          (wildcard last)
DELETE /:id              → PostController.deletePost           (wildcard last)
```

This is a one-line-reordering fix that restores the tag-filtering feature.

### Impact

- The "Browse by Tag" / genre-filtering feature is completely broken
- Any client code that calls `GET /api/v1/post/tag/:tag` gets incorrect results
- The entire `getPostsByTag` controller/service chain (~30 lines of tested code) is dead code with no way to exercise it
- Users cannot browse stories by genre/tag

### Environment

- **File**: `backend/src/app/modules/post/post.router.ts` (lines 43-51)
- **Branch**: `main`
- **Framework**: Express.js

### Record

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct
- [x] I want to work on this issue

Hey @ronisarkarexe! I'm a GSSoC'26 contributor and would like to work on this bug. The fix is a simple route reordering in `post.router.ts`. Please assign me! 🚀

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

Bookmarks are stored in two places that must be kept in sync by hand:

- The `Bookmark` collection (`userId`, `storyId`), used by `bookmark.service.ts`.
- A `bookmarks` array of user ids on each `Post`, used by `post.service.ts` `toggleBookmark` and read by the frontend.

`bookmark.service.toggleBookmark` writes both: it creates/deletes a `Bookmark` document and then separately updates `Post.bookmarks`. Each operation is now individually atomic (an earlier fix replaced the old non-atomic `save()`), but the two writes are still not atomic together. If the process fails between them, the two stores diverge. There is also a second, parallel toggle (`post.service.toggleBookmark`, mounted at `POST /post/bookmark/:id`) that only updates `Post.bookmarks` and never touches the `Bookmark` collection, so the two endpoints can produce inconsistent state for the same post.

This is related to the already-resolved concurrency fixes in #1009 / #991, but those addressed atomicity of the individual counters, not the dual source of truth itself.

This maps to CWE-doubled-state / data-integrity (denormalized data kept consistent only by application code).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Bookmark a story through the bookmark endpoint, then inspect both `Bookmark` documents and that post's `bookmarks` array; they are kept in sync only by sequential writes.
2. Toggle the same post through `POST /post/bookmark/:id`, which updates only `Post.bookmarks`, and observe the `Bookmark` collection is now out of step.

### Environment (if relevant)

- Files: `bookmark.service.ts`, `post.service.ts`, `post.model.ts`, `user.service.ts`, plus the frontend `BookmarkButton` and bookmark-count UI.

### Suggested fix

Make the `Bookmark` collection the single source of truth and replace the `Post.bookmarks` array with a denormalized `bookmarksCount` integer:

- Both backend toggles operate on the `Bookmark` collection and atomically `$inc` `Post.bookmarksCount`.
- The frontend derives the per-user bookmarked state from the existing `GET /bookmarks/status/:storyId` endpoint instead of scanning an array, and reads `bookmarksCount` for display.
- A one-time migration backfills existing `Post.bookmarks` arrays into `Bookmark` documents and sets `bookmarksCount`.

A PR implementing this, including the migration script, is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A.

payload.author: Anexus5919
payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

`backend/src/app.ts` schedules a monthly cron to reset `requestsThisMonth`, but it is wrapped in `if (!process.env.VERCEL)`, so it never runs on the Vercel serverless deployment. Even off Vercel it would not run reliably, because serverless and most process-per-request hosts do not keep a long-lived process alive to fire `node-cron`.

```ts
if (!process.env.VERCEL) {
  cron.schedule("0 0 1 * *", async () => {
    await User.updateMany({}, { $set: { requestsThisMonth: 0 } });
  });
}
```

The important part: this cron is not actually needed. The real monthly reset is already handled lazily and correctly inside `reserveUserQuota` (`quota.service.ts`). Its `effectiveCountExpression` uses a `$cond` that treats `requestsThisMonth` as 0 whenever `lastRequestDate` is null or older than the first day of the current month. So a user whose stored count is left over from last month is correctly treated as having 0 used this month the moment they next generate, regardless of the cron. `requestsThisMonth` is never read directly for enforcement or shown to users (it is only referenced in tests), so the stored value being stale has no effect.

The legacy non-atomic reset that used to live in `ai_model.service.ts` has already been removed, so the cron is the only remaining reference to the old approach and is now misleading dead code: it implies a scheduled reset happens when, on the actual deployment, it does not.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy on Vercel (or any serverless host). `process.env.VERCEL` is set, so the cron is never scheduled.
2. Confirm via `reserveUserQuota` that the monthly limit still resets correctly anyway, because `effectiveCountExpression` zeroes last-month usage on the next request.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `backend/src/app.ts`
- Quota logic: `backend/src/app/modules/ai_model/quota.service.ts`

### Suggested fix

Remove the dead cron block and its now-unused imports (`node-cron`, `User`, `NewsletterSubscriber`) from `app.ts`. The lazy `$cond` reset in `reserveUserQuota` is authoritative and unchanged, so enforcement behavior is identical. A separate Vercel Cron Job would only be worth adding if a stored, eagerly-reset counter is ever needed for display, which is not the case today.

A PR removing the dead cron is attached. The `node-cron` dependency removal is left out of this PR to avoid a lockfile change while the lockfile is already out of sync (tracked in #1161 / #1534); it can be dropped from `package.json` in that cleanup.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A.

payload.author: Anexus5919
payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

Three unauthenticated POST endpoints have no rate limiting, so a single client can flood them.

- `POST /api/v1/bug-reports/submit` (`bug_report.router.ts`): anyone can insert unlimited bug report documents.
- `POST /api/v1/contact` (`contact.route.ts`): each request sends an email via SMTP, so flooding it both spams the support inbox and abuses the mail credentials.
- `POST /api/v1/newsletter/subscribe` (`newsletter.route.ts`): each request triggers a verification email via SMTP, same email-abuse and inbox-flood vector, and can be used to mail-bomb arbitrary addresses.

These endpoints are intentionally public (anonymous users can legitimately use them), so the fix is rate limiting rather than authentication.

This is different from #1043, which is about rate limiting the payment order endpoint specifically. The serverless-safe MongoDB-backed rate limiter added in #1519 / #1520 is already on `main`, so these endpoints can reuse it directly.

This maps to CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Without authenticating, send many requests in a loop to any of the three endpoints, for example:
   ```
   for i in $(seq 1 50); do
     curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST \
       https://apistorysparkai.vercel.app/api/v1/newsletter/subscribe \
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email":"victim@example.com"}'
   done
   ```
2. Observe that none are throttled, and for contact/newsletter each accepted request sends an email.

### Environment (if relevant)

- Files: `bug_report.router.ts`, `contact.route.ts`, `newsletter.route.ts`

### Suggested fix

Mount the existing `createRateLimiter` factory (from `ip.rate-limiter.ts`, MongoDB-backed and serverless-safe) on each endpoint with its own key prefix: bug report 10 per hour, contact 5 per hour, newsletter subscribe 5 per hour. The email-sending endpoints get a tighter limit since they are the credential-abuse vector.

A PR is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. The loop above is sufficient proof.

payload.author: Anexus5919
payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

Several user-writable text fields have no maximum length at either the validation layer or the database schema, so an authenticated user can store arbitrarily large strings and bloat the database.

- `backend/src/app/modules/comment/comment.validation.ts`: `comment` enforces only `min(1)`, no upper bound.
- `backend/src/app/modules/comment/comment.model.ts`: `comment` field has no `maxlength`.
- `backend/src/app/modules/user/user.model.ts`: `profile.bio`, `profile.avatar`, and the `social.*` fields have no `maxlength`.
- `backend/src/app/modules/user/user.validation.ts`: `updateUser` accepts `bio`, `avatar`, and `social.*` as unbounded strings.

This is the same class of problem as #1296 (which covers post `title` and `content`), but for the comment and profile surfaces, which that issue does not mention. Even with an Express body-size limit in place, each request can still persist megabytes of text per field, and a `maxlength` at the Mongoose layer provides defense in depth if a write path ever bypasses the Zod validator.

This maps to CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Authenticate as any user.
2. Send `POST /api/v1/comment/create` with a `comment` field containing several megabytes of text, or `PATCH /api/v1/user/update` with a multi-megabyte `profile.bio`.
3. Observe the value is accepted and stored unbounded.

### Environment (if relevant)

Backend: Node.js / Express / Mongoose / Zod

### Suggested fix

Add generous upper bounds at both the Zod and Mongoose layers (well above normal usage): comment 5000, bio 1000, avatar/url 2000, social handles 200. Apply the same approach to the post fields from #1296 (title 200, content 50000, tag 50, etc.).

A PR covering both this and #1296 is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. This is a server-side validation gap.

### Record

### Is there an existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Describe the feature

Feature Description

When reading a published story on /post/:id, there is currently no visual indicator of how far through the story the reader is. For longer AI-generated stories this makes it hard to know if you're near the beginning, middle, or end.

I'd like to add a thin fixed progress bar at the top of the viewport that fills as you scroll through the story — a pattern used by Medium, DEV.to, Substack, and most modern reading platforms.

Current Behaviour

Visiting any story page (/post/:id) and scrolling through shows no reading progress indicator anywhere.

Verified by checking the codebase directly:

frontend/src/components/post/post.details.component.tsx

Zero scroll-related logic, no useEffect with a scroll listener, no progress state exists in this file. The useState imports only cover isEditing, editedTitle, editedContent, and showTimeline — nothing related to reading progress.

Proposed Behaviour

A 4px tall indigo bar fixed to the top of the page that grows from 0% → 100% width as the user scrolls from the top to the bottom of the story. Resets to 0% when navigating to a new post.

Implementation Plan

File to change: frontend/src/components/post/post.details.component.tsx

  1. Add a readProgress numeric state variable to the component
  2. Add a useEffect that attaches a passive scroll listener on mount and calculates scroll percentage based on scrollTop and scrollHeight
  3. Clean up the scroll listener in the useEffect return to prevent memory leaks when navigating away
  4. Add a fixed, full-width progress bar element at the top of the JSX that reads from the readProgress state and uses the existing indigo-500 accent colour to stay consistent with the component's design

Why This Matters

  • StorySpark generates stories of varying lengths —> readers currently have no sense of how long the read is once they're in it
  • It's a ~20 line change with high visible impact
  • Fully accessible — > uses correct ARIA progressbar role with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax
  • Passive scroll listener = zero performance cost
  • Matches the existing design language —> indigo accent, consistent with the rest of the component
  • Standard UX on every major reading platform (Medium, DEV.to, Substack, Hashnode)

📋 Checklist (if assigned)

  • [ ] Add readProgress state and useEffect scroll listener with passive: true flag
  • [ ] Add progress bar div with ARIA progressbar role
  • [ ] Verify bar resets to 0% when navigating between posts (cleanup in useEffect return)
  • [ ] Test on mobile (touch scroll)
  • [ ] Test in both light mode and dark mode
  • [ ] Verify it doesn't overlap the existing navbar

File

File | Change -- | -- frontend/src/components/post/post.details.component.tsx | Add scroll listener + progress bar JSX

Can I be assigned this issue? I've identified the exact file, confirmed nothing similar exists in the codebase or open issues, and have the full implementation ready to go.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

While reviewing the AudioPlayer component, I noticed a few stability and accessibility issues that impact performance and markup validity:
1)Stale Closure / High-Frequency Ref Updates: The useImperativeHandle hook includes speech.currentWordIndex in its dependency array. Because this index updates rapidly on every spoken word, the ref object is completely re-allocated and assigned constantly during playback.
2)Invalid Semantics: Native <select> elements are explicitly given role="combobox". According to WAI-ARIA standards, a native select represents a listbox structure. Forcing a combobox role without an input/popup pattern breaks accessibility trees.


### Steps to reproduce

1. High-Frequency Ref Allocation Bug (useImperativeHandle)
Steps to Reproduce:
Open the component in an environment with React Developer Tools installed.

In the parent component containing AudioPlayer, grab a reference to the player using a standard React ref:

TypeScript
const playerRef = useRef<AudioPlayerHandle>(null);
<AudioPlayer ref={playerRef} text="A long story with many words..." />
Set up a useEffect hook in the parent component that tracks changes to playerRef.current.

Click Play to start the narration.

Watch the console or the React DevTools profile.

Expected Behavior:
The imperative handle interface (stop) should remain a stable object reference throughout playback.

Actual Behavior:
The playerRef.current object mutates and re-allocates on every single word boundary change, causing unnecessary ref churn.

2. Invalid HTML Semantics (role="combobox")
Steps to Reproduce:
Right-click on the Playback speed, Narration language, or Voice dropdown menu in your browser.

Select Inspect to open the browser's Developer Tools HTML tree.

Observe the generated element: <select role="combobox" ...>

Run an accessibility audit tool like Lighthouse, Axe DevTools, or an HTML validator (e.g., Nu HTML Checker) on the page.

Expected Behavior:
Native <select> elements carry an implicit role="listbox" and pass standard accessibility/HTML5 validation.

Actual Behavior:
The validator or accessibility tree flags an error: An element with role="combobox" must be a composite widget containing an input field.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The profile update endpoint allows authenticated users to modify privileged account fields that should not be user-controlled.

A normal user can update fields such as `role` and `subscriptionType` through the profile update API. Since authentication tokens are generated using values stored in the database, the modified role is reflected in newly issued tokens.

As a result, a standard user can obtain elevated permissions that should only be granted through authorized administrative workflows.

### Expected Behavior

Regular users should only be able to update their own profile information.

Authorization-related fields such as roles, permissions, and subscription status should not be modifiable through the self-service profile update endpoint.

### Actual Behavior

The endpoint accepts privileged fields from authenticated users and persists them, allowing users to gain access to functionality intended for higher-privileged roles.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Register or log in as a normal user account.
2. Send a profile update request to the user update endpoint.
3. Include privileged fields such as:

   * `role`
   * `subscriptionType`
4. Submit the request successfully.
5. Log in again or obtain a new access token.
6. Observe that the updated role is reflected in the account permissions and token claims.

**What should exist:**
The backend feed query and frontend infinite scroll should rely on cursor-based pagination instead of offset-based pagination.

**Who uses it:**
All users scrolling through the global story feed.

**What problem it solves:**
Currently, fetching the list of stories relies on standard offset-based pagination (using `skip` and `limit`). As the platform's `posts` collection grows, `skip` becomes highly inefficient because the database must scan and discard all preceding documents. Additionally, offset pagination can cause duplicate or missed posts if new stories are inserted at the top of the feed while a user is scrolling.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

### What would you like to improve?

## Summary

Two authentication-related issues were identified:

1. The authentication middleware did not properly parse `Authorization: Bearer <token>` headers.

Together, these issues could prevent authenticated requests from succeeding and cause user registration or password hashing failures.

---

### Reproduction

1. Obtain a valid JWT.
2. Send a request to a protected endpoint with:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

3. Observe that the request is rejected as unauthorized.

### Expected Behavior

The middleware should extract the token from the Bearer header and verify only the JWT value.

### Actual Behavior

The middleware attempts to verify the entire header value (`Bearer <token>`), causing JWT verification to fail.

### Impact

Most HTTP clients, browsers, mobile applications, and API tools send authentication credentials using the Bearer scheme. As a result, authenticated routes fail despite valid tokens.

### Location

```
auth.middleware.ts
```

### Proposed Fix

* Strip the optional `Bearer ` prefix.
* Trim whitespace before verification.
* Continue supporting raw token values where applicable.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

## Summary

When `SALT_ROUNDS` is unset or contains an invalid value, the application may pass `NaN` to bcrypt during password hashing. This can cause user registration and password-related operations to fail unexpectedly.

## Expected Behavior

- If `SALT_ROUNDS` is missing, the server should use a safe default value of `10`.
- If `SALT_ROUNDS` is invalid (non-numeric, empty, negative, etc.), the server should fall back to `10`.
- Password hashing should continue without throwing errors.

## Actual Behavior

- Invalid configuration can result in `NaN` being passed to bcrypt, causing password hashing and user registration to fail.
## Proposed Fix

- Validate the parsed value of `SALT_ROUNDS`.
- Fallback to a default value of `10` whenever the environment variable is missing or invalid.
- Add automated tests covering:
  - Missing `SALT_ROUNDS`
  - Invalid `SALT_ROUNDS`
  - Valid `SALT_ROUNDS`

## Changed Files

- Authentication/password hashing configuration file(s)
- Environment configuration handling
- Associated unit/integration test files
- `.env.example` (if documenting the default value)

### Steps to reproduce

### Case 1: SALT_ROUNDS unset

1. Remove `SALT_ROUNDS` from the environment configuration.
2. Start the server.
3. Attempt to register a new user.
4. Observe that bcrypt receives an invalid rounds value and hashing may fail.

### Case 2: SALT_ROUNDS invalid

1. Set:
   ```env
   SALT_ROUNDS=invalid
   ```
2. Start the server.
3. Attempt to register a new user.
4. Observe that bcrypt receives `NaN` instead of a valid integer.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The bookmarks list endpoint populates user emails into its response, the same class of PII leak as #1512 but in a different file that the related PR did not touch.

`backend/src/app/modules/bookmark/bookmark.service.ts`, in `getBookmarks`:

```
populate: [
  { path: "author", select: "name email createdAt profile.bio" },
  { path: "reactions", populate: { path: "userId", select: "email" } },
  { path: "bookmarks", select: "email" },
],
```

So `GET /api/v1/bookmarks` returns, for each saved story, the author's email, every reactor's email, and the email of every other user who bookmarked that story. Even though the endpoint requires login, it hands the caller other users' personal emails (notably every co-bookmarker), which they have no reason to receive.

This maps to CWE-359 (Exposure of Private Personal Information).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Log in and save a story that other users have also bookmarked or reacted to.
2. Call `GET /api/v1/bookmarks`.
3. Inspect the response. Each story's `author.email`, `reactions[].userId.email`, and `bookmarks[].email` contain other users' email addresses.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `backend/src/app/modules/bookmark/bookmark.service.ts`
- Endpoint: `GET /api/v1/bookmarks`

### Suggested fix

Return the opaque `_id` instead of `email` in all three populated relations, matching the fix for the post endpoints in #1512. The frontend computes ownership, like, and bookmark state from these relations, so it should compare `_id` (the shared `_id` identity migration). This is handled together with #1512 in the same PR, since they share that frontend change.

payload.author: Anexus5919
payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

Two related auth weaknesses around refresh tokens.

1. No refresh-token rotation or reuse detection. `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh-token` (`auth.service.ts` `refreshToken`) only mints a new access token. The long-lived refresh token is never rotated, and there is no server-side record of issued refresh tokens, so a stolen refresh token can be replayed for its full lifetime and the theft cannot be detected. RFC 6819 section 5.2.2.3 recommends rotating the refresh token on each use and treating reuse of a retired token as a compromise signal.

2. Password reset does not invalidate existing sessions, and its auto-login tokens are broken. The token versioning mechanism added in PR #811 (issue #635) handles `change-password`, but the forgot-password `resetPassword` path was left out:
   - It never increments `tokenVersion`, so sessions that existed before the reset stay valid. This is exactly the vulnerability #635 set out to fix (step 3, "Invalidate Existing Sessions on Password Reset"), still present for the reset path.
   - The auto-login tokens it returns omit `tokenVersion` entirely. The auth middleware compares `user.tokenVersion` (0) against the token's `tokenVersion` (undefined), so `0 !== undefined` is true and the very next protected request returns 401. Auto-login after a password reset is currently broken.

This maps to CWE-613 (Insufficient Session Expiration) and CWE-384 (Session Fixation / reuse).

### Steps to reproduce

Rotation:
1. Log in. Call `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh-token`. Only a new access token is returned; the same refresh token keeps working indefinitely, with no rotation and no reuse detection.

Reset path:
1. Complete the forgot-password flow and reset the password.
2. The response includes an access token, but the first protected API call with it returns 401 because the token has no `tokenVersion`.
3. Separately, any token issued before the reset still works, so the reset did not end existing sessions.

### Environment (if relevant)

- Files: `backend/src/app/modules/auth/auth.service.ts`, `auth.controller.ts`, `auth.router.ts`, `backend/src/utils/cookie.util.ts`

### Suggested fix

- Persist issued refresh tokens with a unique id (jti) in a MongoDB collection with a TTL index.
- On refresh, rotate: validate the token, mark its record used, issue a new access and a new refresh token, and set the new refresh cookie. If a refresh token that was already used is presented again, treat it as theft and revoke the whole family plus bump `tokenVersion`.
- Read the refresh token from the httpOnly cookie (it is set as a cookie, but the endpoint was reading the Authorization header, which the client cannot supply for an httpOnly cookie).
- In `resetPassword`, increment `tokenVersion` and include it in the issued tokens, so reset both invalidates old sessions and produces working auto-login tokens.
- Add a `logout` endpoint that revokes the current refresh session and clears the cookie.

A PR implementing all of this is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. These are code-level auth weaknesses.

### Record

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct
- [x] I want to work on this issue

payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

Collaboration room IDs are generated with a non-cryptographic PRNG, so they are short and guessable.

`backend/src/socket/collab.socket.ts`:

```
function generateRoomId(): string {
  return Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 10);
}
```

That is 8 base-36 characters derived from `Math.random()`, roughly 41 bits of weak, non-cryptographic entropy. Because `collab:join_room` admits any authenticated user who presents a valid room ID (the room ID is effectively the capability that grants access), a weak ID means an attacker can guess or brute-force room IDs and drop into a private writing session: read the in-progress story and trigger `collab:ai_continue`, which consumes a participant's monthly AI quota.

This is different from #945, which was about user identity spoofing in the websocket handshake (a separate layer that has been fixed). This issue is specifically the predictability of the room ID itself.

This maps to CWE-338 (Use of Cryptographically Weak PRNG) and CWE-330 (Use of Insufficiently Random Values).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Read `backend/src/socket/collab.socket.ts`. Room IDs come from `Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 10)`.
2. Because the keyspace is small and non-cryptographic, room IDs are feasible to guess or enumerate, and `collab:join_room` grants access to anyone who presents a valid ID.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `backend/src/socket/collab.socket.ts`
- Socket.IO namespace: `/collab`

### Suggested fix

Generate the room ID with a cryptographically secure RNG so it becomes an unguessable capability:

```
import crypto from "crypto";

function generateRoomId(): string {
  return crypto.randomBytes(16).toString("hex"); // 128-bit
}
```

With an unguessable ID, the existing share-the-link model is safe against guessing and enumeration. A separate, explicit invite or allowlist system (so a leaked link cannot be reused) would be a reasonable future enhancement, but it needs a frontend invite flow, so it is out of scope here. A backend-only PR for the room ID is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. This is a code-level randomness weakness.

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The newsletter module still exposes two unauthenticated POST routes that let anyone unsubscribe, or probe for, any email address.

`backend/src/app/modules/newsletter/newsletter.route.ts`:

```
router.post("/subscribe", subscribe);
router.get("/verify/:token", verify);
router.post("/unsubscribe", unsubscribe);            // takes a raw email
router.post("/unsubscribe-token", generateUnsubscribeToken);  // mints a token for any email
router.get("/unsubscribe/:token", unsubscribeByToken);
```

- `POST /unsubscribe` accepts `{ email }` and unsubscribes that address directly, with no authentication and no proof of ownership. Anyone can unsubscribe anyone.
- `POST /unsubscribe-token` accepts `{ email }` and returns a valid unsubscribe token for that address, so an attacker can mint a token for a victim and then call the GET to unsubscribe them. Same effect, two steps.
- Both also leak subscriber existence: they return `Subscriber not found` for unknown emails versus a success message for known ones, which is email enumeration.

This is a regression from #999 / PR #1001, which added the safe token based `GET /unsubscribe/:token` but left the old insecure POST routes mounted.

This maps to CWE-639 (Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key) and CWE-204 (Observable Response Discrepancy).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Unsubscribe any address with no auth:
   ```
   curl -X POST https://apistorysparkai.vercel.app/api/v1/newsletter/unsubscribe \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email":"victim@example.com"}'
   ```
2. Or mint a token for any address, then call the GET with it:
   ```
   curl -X POST https://apistorysparkai.vercel.app/api/v1/newsletter/unsubscribe-token \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"email":"victim@example.com"}'
   ```
3. Compare responses for a known versus unknown email to confirm the enumeration discrepancy.

### Important: the safe GET route is currently unreachable

While fixing this I found that no email ever delivers an unsubscribe token. The verification email only contains the verify link, and `verificationToken` is cleared after verification, so an active subscriber holds no token. The only way to obtain an unsubscribe token today is the insecure `POST /unsubscribe-token`. So simply deleting the POST routes would leave unsubscribe with no working path at all. The fix needs to deliver a real unsubscribe link by email.

### Suggested fix

1. Delete `POST /unsubscribe` and `POST /unsubscribe-token` and their controller/service functions.
2. Add a persistent `unsubscribeToken` to the subscriber, generated at subscribe time and not cleared on verify.
3. Include an unsubscribe link pointing at `GET /api/v1/newsletter/unsubscribe/:token` in the email, and have that route look the subscriber up by the persistent token.

A PR implementing this is attached.

### Environment (if relevant)

- API host: `apistorysparkai.vercel.app`
- Files: `backend/src/app/modules/newsletter/newsletter.route.ts`, `newsletter.controller.ts`, `newsletter.service.ts`, `newsletter.model.ts`, `backend/src/utils/email.util.ts`

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The Google OAuth login verifies the ID token signature but never checks the `email_verified` claim before trusting the email.

`backend/src/app/modules/auth/auth.service.ts`, in `googleLogin`:

```
const payload_data = ticket.getPayload();
if (!payload_data || !payload_data.email) {
  throw new ApiError(httpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Invalid Google token");
}

const { email, name: googleName, picture } = payload_data;
let user = await User.findOne({ email });
// ... creates / logs in the user keyed only by email
```

Google's OIDC payload includes `email_verified` precisely because an email present in a token is not proof of ownership. With a Google Workspace, an admin can create accounts with arbitrary, unverified email addresses. If `email_verified` is not checked, someone could obtain a validly signed Google ID token carrying an email they do not own and have this backend create or log into an account under that email. Since accounts here are keyed by email, that is an account takeover and impersonation vector.

This maps to CWE-287 (Improper Authentication).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Read `backend/src/app/modules/auth/auth.service.ts` `googleLogin`. After `verifyIdToken`, only `payload_data.email` is checked, not `payload_data.email_verified`.
2. In a test setup with your own client id, present a validly signed Google ID token whose payload has `email_verified: false`. The server still creates or logs in the user.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `backend/src/app/modules/auth/auth.service.ts` (`googleLogin`)
- Endpoint: `POST /api/v1/auth/google-login`

### Suggested fix

Reject the login when the email is not verified, right after the existing payload check:

```
if (!payload_data.email_verified) {
  throw new ApiError(httpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, "Google email is not verified");
}
```

`google-auth-library` exposes `email_verified` on the token payload, so this is a small, well-typed guard. A PR is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. This is a code-level authentication weakness.

payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The shared JWT verification helper does not pin an algorithm, so it accepts whatever the token's `alg` header claims.

`backend/src/utils/jwt.helper.ts`:

```
const verifyToken = (token: string, secret: Secret): JwtPayload => {
  return jwt.verify(token, secret) as JwtPayload;
};
```

Every token check in the app routes through this one helper (`auth.middleware.ts`, `check.request.limit.ts`, `token.ts`, the refresh-token path in `auth.service.ts`, the Socket.IO handshake in `server.ts`, and the collab namespace in `collab.socket.ts`), so the missing pin affects all of them.

Tokens are signed with HS256 (`createToken` uses the default, `createResetToken` sets HS256 explicitly). Without an `algorithms` allowlist on verify, the verifier honors the attacker-controlled `alg` header. `jsonwebtoken` v9 closed the `none` loophole, but not pinning still leaves the door open to algorithm-confusion and downgrade issues if an asymmetric key path is ever introduced, and it is simply not defense in depth. Pinning the algorithm is the standard hardening step and costs one line.

This maps to CWE-347 (Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Read `backend/src/utils/jwt.helper.ts`. `verifyToken` calls `jwt.verify(token, secret)` with no `algorithms` option.
2. The verifier therefore does not restrict which algorithm a presented token may use.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `backend/src/utils/jwt.helper.ts`
- Affects all auth-protected REST routes and both Socket.IO namespaces, since they all use this helper.

### Suggested fix

Pin the algorithm on verify, and set it explicitly on sign so the two never drift:

```
// sign
const options = { algorithm: "HS256", expiresIn: expireTime } as SignOptions;

// verify
return jwt.verify(token, secret, { algorithms: ["HS256"] }) as JwtPayload;
```

Because every call site delegates to this helper, this single change covers all of them. A one-line-per-function PR is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. This is a code-level cryptographic hardening change.

### Record

- [x] I want to work on this issue

payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The email verification and password reset OTP is generated with `Math.random()`, which is not cryptographically secure.

`backend/src/app/modules/verify_email/verify_email.service.ts`:

```
const otp = Math.floor(100000 + Math.random() * 900000).toString();
```

`Math.random()` is backed by V8's xorshift128+ PRNG, which is seeded once per process and is not designed to be unpredictable. An attacker who observes a few legitimate outputs from the same Node process can recover the internal PRNG state and predict subsequent values. On a serverless cold start the available entropy is also low. Because this same OTP is used both for signup verification and for the password reset flow, a predictable OTP weakens account takeover protection.

This is different from #946, which was about rate limiting the OTP send endpoints, not the quality of the random number. It is also different from #1275, which is about the guest user id using `Math.random()` in a different file.

This maps to CWE-338 (Use of Cryptographically Weak PRNG).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Read `backend/src/app/modules/verify_email/verify_email.service.ts`.
2. The OTP is `Math.floor(100000 + Math.random() * 900000)`, which derives a security-sensitive code from a non-cryptographic PRNG.

### Environment (if relevant)

- File: `backend/src/app/modules/verify_email/verify_email.service.ts`
- Affects both the signup email verification and the forgot/reset password OTP flows.

### Suggested fix

Use Node's cryptographically secure RNG. `crypto` is already imported in this file:

```
const otp = crypto.randomInt(100000, 1000000).toString();
```

`crypto.randomInt(100000, 1000000)` returns an integer in `[100000, 1000000)`, i.e. 100000 to 999999, which is the same 6-digit range as before, so nothing downstream changes.

A one-line PR is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. This is a code-level cryptographic weakness.

payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The authentication and free-AI rate limiters keep their state in a per-process in-memory `Map`, so they do not work on the Vercel serverless deployment.

- `backend/src/app/middleware/ip.rate-limiter.ts` uses `const store = new Map(...)` for the login, registration, forgot-password, and reset-password limiters.
- `backend/src/app/middleware/free-ai.rate-limiter.ts` uses the same in-memory `Map` for guest AI generations.

On Vercel, each serverless function instance has its own memory, and instances are created and destroyed on demand. Requests are spread across many instances, and a cold start begins with an empty `Map`. So the counters are never shared. An attacker can bypass the limits simply by sending requests that land on different or fresh instances. This defeats the protection these limiters were added for: credential stuffing on login, registration and OTP spam, and free-AI abuse.

This is different from #1290, which is about a memory leak (missing cleanup) in `middlewares/rateLimitMiddleware.ts`. That issue assumes a single long-lived process. This issue is that the in-memory approach itself cannot enforce a shared limit on serverless.

This maps to CWE-307 (Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts) and OWASP API4:2023 (Unrestricted Resource Consumption).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Send several requests in quick succession to a limited endpoint, for example forgot-password which is configured for 3 per hour:
   ```
   for i in $(seq 1 8); do
     curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST \
       https://apistorysparkai.vercel.app/api/v1/auth/forgot-password \
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
       -d '{"email":"probe_zzz_99999@example.com"}'
   done
   ```
2. Observe that none of the responses are `429`. With a working 3-per-hour limit, requests after the third should be blocked. I ran this against production and saw eight `404` responses and zero `429`.

### Environment (if relevant)

- API host: `apistorysparkai.vercel.app` (Vercel serverless, see `backend/vercel.json`)
- Files: `backend/src/app/middleware/ip.rate-limiter.ts`, `backend/src/app/middleware/free-ai.rate-limiter.ts`

### Suggested fix

Move the limiter state to a shared store so it holds across all instances. The conventional options are a MongoDB collection with a TTL index, or a managed Redis such as Upstash. Since this project already requires MongoDB and does not have a `REDIS_URL` provisioned (the existing `redis.client.ts` falls back to `127.0.0.1:6379`, which does not exist on Vercel), MongoDB is the lower-risk choice and needs no new infrastructure.

The attached PR adds a shared MongoDB-backed store with a TTL index and rewires both limiters to use it, preserving the exact thresholds and block windows, and failing open if the store is briefly unavailable so a database blip cannot lock users out of auth endpoints.

Related, out of scope here: the global `express-rate-limit` in `app.ts` uses the library's default in-memory store and has the same serverless limitation; and `app.ts` references an unimported `storyRoutes`. Worth separate issues.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. The `curl` loop output above is the proof.

### Record

- [x] I want to work on this issue
payload.title: BUG: In-memory rate limiters do not enforce on Vercel serverless (auth and free-AI limits bypassable)

payload.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The payment flow looks complete but a paid user is never actually upgraded, and the price is trusted from the client.

In `backend/src/controllers/payment.controller.ts`:

1. `verifyPayment` validates the Razorpay HMAC signature correctly and returns `{ success: true, message: "Payment verified successfully" }`, but it never updates the user's `subscriptionType`. No code anywhere in the backend writes `subscriptionType` after user creation, so a user can complete a real Razorpay payment and stay on the free tier.
2. There is no order record. `createOrder` does not persist anything linking `userId` to `razorpay_order_id` and the chosen plan. So even if you wanted to upgrade on verify, the server has no way to know which tier was paid for: the frontend `verify` call only forwards `razorpay_order_id`, `razorpay_payment_id`, and `razorpay_signature`, not the plan.
3. The amount is client controlled. `createOrder` reads `amount` from the request body and creates the Razorpay order with it, so a client can pay any amount they choose for any plan.

This is distinct from #1041, #1042, #1043, and #1298, which are about authentication and rate limiting on the payment routes. None of them address the subscription never being upgraded, the missing order record, or the client controlled amount.

This maps to CWE-840 (Business Logic Errors) and OWASP API6:2023 (Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call `POST /api/v1/payment/create-order` while logged in with a body like `{ "amount": 1 }`. A Razorpay order is created for that exact amount, proving the price is not enforced server side.
2. Complete the signature handshake and call `POST /api/v1/payment/verify`. It returns success.
3. Query the user document or decode a fresh access token after login. `subscriptionType` is still `free`, so no upgrade happened.

### Environment (if relevant)

- API host: `apistorysparkai.vercel.app`
- Files: `backend/src/controllers/payment.controller.ts`, `backend/src/router/payment.route.ts`

### Suggested fix

1. Persist orders. On `create-order`, store `{ userId, razorpayOrderId, plan, amount, currency, status: "created" }`.
2. Resolve the price server side from a plan to price map. Take a `plan` from the client, not an `amount`, so the user cannot set their own price.
3. On `verify`, after the signature passes, atomically claim the order (`status: created -> paid`) and update `User.subscriptionType` to the order's tier. The atomic status transition makes a replayed verify a no-op so a tier cannot be granted twice.
4. As a follow-up, add a Razorpay webhook handler with signature verification so the upgrade still happens if the browser closes before the verify call.

### Additional note (separate frontend bug)

While verifying this, the payment page `frontend/src/components/home/pricing/payment.component.tsx` appears broken on its own: the Razorpay handler `handlePayment` is never called (the form `onSubmit` calls an undefined `handlePay`), and several referenced state values (`name`, `cardNumber`, `cvv`, `loading`, `isFormValid`) are never declared. It also collects raw card fields in a custom form, which Razorpay should handle in its own checkout. This needs a separate frontend fix so the page actually calls `create-order` with a `plan`. The backend fix is correct and ready for whenever that frontend work lands.

A PR implementing items 1 to 3 on the backend is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. Reproduction is via the API calls and decoding the token as described above.

- [x] I want to work on this issue

### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### What happened?

The public post endpoints return personal email addresses of users to anyone, with no authentication. The story author's email, every reactor's email, and every bookmarker's email are serialized into the response.

In `backend/src/app/modules/post/post.service.ts`, every read query populates user relations with `email`:

```
.populate("author", "name email createdAt profile.bio")
.populate({ path: "reactions", populate: { path: "userId", select: "email" } })
.populate("bookmarks", "email");
```

This pattern repeats in `getPosts`, `getPublishedPostsByAuthor`, `getLatestPosts`, `getFeaturedPosts`, `getSinglePost`, and `getPostsByTag`. The routes `GET /post/lists`, `GET /post/latest-lists`, `GET /post/feature-lists`, `GET /post/:id`, and `GET /post/tag/:tag` have no auth middleware, so the emails are exposed to unauthenticated clients. Pagination via the `page` query param lets an attacker walk the entire user base.

This is distinct from the closed `/users` endpoint issues (#658, #617, #613). Those covered the user list and single user routes. This is the post listing surface, which leaks the same class of PII through a different path.

This maps to CWE-359 (Exposure of Private Personal Information) and OWASP API3:2023 (Broken Object Property Level Authorization / excessive data exposure).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call the public list endpoint with no auth:
   ```
   curl -s "https://apistorysparkai.vercel.app/api/v1/post/lists?limit=10"
   ```
2. Observe each item contains `author.email` with a real personal email address. Reactions and bookmarks also carry user emails.
3. Increase `page` to enumerate further. At the time of filing, `meta.total` was over 100 posts, exposing the email of every author.

### Environment (if relevant)

- API host: `apistorysparkai.vercel.app`
- File: `backend/src/app/modules/post/post.service.ts`
- Verified live on production at the time of filing (returned real Gmail addresses).

### Suggested fix

Stop returning any user email from public post payloads. Return the opaque `_id` instead, which is not PII:

```
.populate("author", "name createdAt profile.bio")
.populate({ path: "reactions", populate: { path: "userId", select: "_id" } })
.populate("bookmarks", "_id");
```

This requires a small frontend change because the UI currently uses these emails to compute post ownership, like state, and bookmark state. Those checks should compare the user `_id` instead. Note that `buildUserInfo` in `frontend/src/services/auth.service.ts` reads `decodedData.userId`, but the JWT only carries `_id`, so `currentUser.userId` is currently always an empty string and the existing `_id` based checks (for example `isAuthor` in `post.details.component.tsx`) are silently dead. Mapping `userId` from the token `_id` fixes that and lets the UI compare by id.

A PR implementing the full fix (backend plus the frontend identity migration) is attached.

### Screenshots or screen recording (if helpful)

N/A. The `curl` response above is sufficient proof.

### Record

- [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct
- [x] I want to work on this issue
